subject: P95 avalanche: decision and mitigation options for model zeta7
messages:
From: Clara Wells <clara.wells@zenith-retail.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@zenith-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 surge since zeta7 -> urgent request

Hi Chloe,

We started seeing large p95 latency spikes across our checkout traffic shortly after the zeta7 variant was promoted on Friday. CPU and concurrency on our side look normal; the user-facing page is timing out for some high-frequency flows.

Attached are a small sample of the token-level latencies (sla-p95-samples.csv) and a couple of request log snippets. The spike began ~17:40 UTC on 2026-10-16 and has persisted in bursts. Our SLA with Redwood explicitly calls out p95 latency and impact >5% may trigger credits.

We need Redwood to either: (A) immediately revert to the previous model variant or (B) temporarily pin traffic off zeta7 and provide a mitigation timeline. We appreciate a quick confirmation of steps you will take and an ETA.

Thanks,
Clara
Clara Wells
Director, Platform Engineering
Zenith Retail

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sudden p95 surge since zeta7 -> urgent request

Chloe / Marissa — quick findings from initial triage:

- Reproduced p95 spike on our canary test harness when running zeta7 with long-sequence checkout prompts. Median token latency is fine; the tail (95-99) shows step increases around kv-cache flushes.
- Kernel traces point to a new attention kernel fallback on A100 machines with mixed-quant config; the fallback coincides with higher memory pressure on long sequences.
- No obvious network routing issues; errors and retry rates are unchanged.

Recommendation and next steps:
1) Immediate: Pin Zenith traffic to the prior variant (zeta6-stable) for 30 minutes to stop user impact. This is a config flip and can be done without a code deploy.
2) Parallel: Rollback window — if pin shows stability, authorize rollback to zeta6 across the account at a low-traffic hour (we recommend 02:00 UTC).
3) Post-action: Collect extended kernel traces and run a quantization regression test matrix to root-cause the fallback.

Risk/contract: rollback will change the served model; if Zenith wants Redwood to proceed without a signed change order, we need explicit written consent (email ok) because billing/variant lock is documented in the contract.

I’ve attached a short runtime trace page for ops (postmortem-trace.html) and marked the suspect kernel calls. If leadership (Jonas / Marissa) approves, we can flip the pin now.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Clara / Procurement team — following our triage and Ben’s findings, here is the mitigation path we propose. Apologies again for the impact.

Summary of recommended actions (safe-first approach):
1) Immediate traffic pin to zeta6-stable (no deploy) — reduces exposure within 5 minutes and preserves recent traffic routing.
2) Observe for 1 hour. If p95 returns to baseline, schedule account rollback to zeta6 at 02:00 UTC on 2026-10-21 (low traffic window). Rollback is a standard operational change but we require explicit customer go-ahead per contract.
3) Root-cause analysis to be delivered within 72 hours with kernel correlation and mitigations (code/quant fix or a config guard).

Please reply with a short authorization: “Redwood authorized to pin and schedule rollback to zeta6 on 2026-10-21 at 02:00 UTC” or indicate you prefer only the pin for now. If you’d like us to proceed immediately with both steps we can start the formal rollback process and route paperwork to Procurement.

If we do not receive written authorization within 2 hours, we will proceed with the pin only to protect your production traffic.

Sincerely,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
